outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the lower bound has moved in many dimensions outside 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 and 24 (11, 12, 17 to 21, 25 to 31, and claimed values in 38, 39, 43, 45 and 55), and one upper bound moved (dimension 6 to 77, April 2024), but no kissing number outside {1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 24} has been determined exactly.
problem_asks: The statement asks for the kissing number k(n), the maximum number of non-overlapping unit spheres that can touch a central unit sphere in R^n, for every dimension n except 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 and 24. Parts: (a) for each such n, determine k(n) exactly; the statement names no particular n, so it is a family of separate sub-questions, one per dimension; (b) implicit in (a), the lower-bound side (constructions) and the upper-bound side (proofs) for each n, since determining k(n) needs both to meet. The statement names no asymptotic quantity. The exclusions (1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 24) are the dimensions where k(n) is already known.

events.what_happened: Mikhail Ganzhinov, 'Highly symmetric lines' (arXiv:2207.08266). Gives three new kissing configurations improving lower bounds to 510 (d=10), 592 (d=11) and 1932 (d=14), built from highly symmetric line systems (twisted spherical functions of finite groups; for d=14 a representation of U(3,3)). Predates the frozen revision. Published as Linear Algebra and its Applications vol. 722 (2025), per a search snippet of the Aalto portal; that journal entry was not opened. The 2025 publication is not treated as the event date.
events.revisions: Single version v1, 17 Jul 2022 (arXiv abstract page read).
events.delivers: Lower bounds only: 510 in d=10, 592 in d=11, 1932 in d=14. Three dimensions in scope; no exact value and no upper bound.
events.remains: The exact kissing number in every dimension in scope, including 10, 11 and 14; the d=11 bound was later raised to 593 (AlphaEvolve) and 604 (EinsteinArena agents).

events.what_happened: Nando M. Leijenhorst and David de Laat, 'Solving clustered low-rank semidefinite programs arising from polynomial optimization' (arXiv:2202.12077), with a computational application to three-point semidefinite (Bachoc-Vallentin) upper bounds for kissing numbers. A search summary says this allows improved kissing-number upper bounds in dimensions 11 to 23, published as Mathematical Programming Computation 16(3), 503-534 (2024). Predates the frozen revision. Not opened; known only from search snippets and from the upper-bound credits in Cohn's table.

events.remains: The exact kissing number in every dimension in scope; the upper bounds stay well above the lower bounds in every dimension from 9 upward.
events.doubts: Numbers attributed to this work come from Cohn's table and a search summary; I did not read the paper, so the 868, 1355 and 3174 figures are not verified against it.

events.what_happened: David de Laat, Nando M. Leijenhorst and Willem H. H. de Muinck Keizer, 'Optimality and uniqueness of the D4 root system' (arXiv:2404.18794). Proves the D4 root system is the unique optimal kissing configuration in R^4 (dimension 4, excluded from the problem) and states that it improves the upper bound for the kissing number in R^6 to 77. Dimension 6 is in scope. The abstract was read; the full text was not.
events.delivers: Upper bound 77 on the kissing number in dimension 6 (lower bound 72 per Cohn's table). Upper bound only, in one dimension. Dimension 4 uniqueness is out of scope.
events.remains: The exact kissing number in dimension 6 (72 to 77 per Cohn's table) and every other dimension in scope.
events.doubts: The abstract says the method uses an exact optimal solution to the second level of the Lasserre hierarchy computed by semidefinite programming. I did not check whether the computation is certified exactly or only numerically.
events.direction: Upper-bound side only, dimension 6. Cuts against no conjecture; it lowers an upper bound and does not determine k(6).

events.what_happened: Henry Cohn and Anqi Li, 'Improved kissing numbers in seventeen through twenty-one dimensions' (arXiv:2411.04916). Lower bounds 5730, 7654, 11692, 19448 and 29768 for d=17 to 21, improving Leech's 1967 records by 384, 256, 1024, 2048 and 2048. The construction changes signs of Leech-lattice vectors (an odd number of minus signs) instead of taking cross-sections. Quanta reported it on 15 Jan 2025 (excerpt only, not opened).
events.revisions: v1 7 Nov 2024; v2 21 Mar 2026; v3 1 Sep 2026 (current; full text read).

events.remains: Exact k(n) for n in 17 to 21 and every other dimension in scope. The later bounds in 18, 19 and 21 (see later events) supersede these values.

The DeepMind blog was not opened; the date comes from a search result and the whataifound registry.

events.what_happened: Chengdong Ma, Théo Tao Zhaowei et al. (nine authors, Yaodong Yang last), 'Finding Kissing Numbers with Game-theoretic Reinforcement Learning' (arXiv:2511.13391). Presents PackingStar, a multi-agent reinforcement learning system that treats the kissing problem as a two-player game. Claims: strictly larger kissing configurations in every dimension from 25 to 31 (surpassing 2016 and 2011 constructions; e.g., K(25) reported as 197056 in its figure); in dimension 13 a rational configuration of 1146 points beating the 1971 rational record of 1130, while the 1999 non-rational 1154 is not surpassed; and many other structures. Predates no part of the window; first version 17 Nov 2025.
events.revisions: v1 17 Nov 2025; v2 21 Jan 2026; v3 11 Feb 2026 (full text read); v4 2 Jun 2026; v5 22 Sep 2026 (abstract page). The v1 claims were not read.
events.delivers: Lower bounds in dimensions 25 to 31 (per the v3 text), and a rational 13-dimensional configuration of 1146 points. The 13-dimensional non-rational record (1154) is not surpassed. No exact values and no optimality proofs.
events.remains: Exact values in every dimension in scope. The authors state: 'A current limitation is that PackingStar cannot provide optimality proofs for these new configurations.' The authors also say optimality of dimension 25 is unproven.
events.directly_checkable: Configurations are finite point sets; the rational 1146 configuration is said to have rational inner products, which would allow exact checking. I did not verify this in the text I read.
events.doubts: The authors' own statements are the only support for the claimed records; the abstract wording changed between versions (see disputes). The rational-cosine claim for the 1146 configuration is from the search snippets and the v3 summary, not verified in full. Its 1154 non-rational comparison is with a 1999 record.
events.direction: Lower-bound side only: dimensions 25 to 31 and a rational 13-dimensional configuration. Moves bounds on the problem's quantity without settling it. The 13-dimensional non-rational record is unchanged.
events.object: Kissing configurations in R^25 to R^31 (and the rational 1146-point configuration in R^13), found by an RL search that builds on Leech-lattice and related constructions. The paper says its 25-dimensional configuration corresponds to a substructure of the Leech lattice and may be optimal, without proof. Whether the coordinates are explicit was not verified.

systems.name: PackingStar
systems.what_it_did: Discovers the kissing configurations in dimensions 25 to 31 and the rational 13-dimensional configuration. The paper describes it as 'a multi-agent reinforcement learning system' with a tree-search learner for Player 1 and a neural-network policy trained by policy gradient for Player 2. It is the authors' own system, not a named language model.
systems.basis_quote: PackingStar discovers new interpretable geometric structures.

events.what_happened: Boon Suan Ho (National University of Singapore), 'A new lower bound for the kissing number in 19 dimensions' (arXiv:2603.10425). Lower bound 11948 in d=19, improving Cohn-Li's 11692 by 256. Uses the Cohn-Li odd-sign construction with an explicit nonlinear binary code of length 19, size 1280 and minimum distance 5 inside the 5-punctured extended binary Golay code. The acknowledgements of v2 state that GPT-5.4 Pro was used in the discovery of the construction.

events.what_happened: Together AI's EinsteinArena platform reports that a collaboration of AI agents raised the dimension-11 lower bound from 593 to 604. The blog says the first agent submission (alpha_omega_agents, 8 April 2026) had overlaps and was not a valid configuration; several agents then refined it over about 48 hours, using LSQR to reduce the overlap loss and integer snapping to finish. A valid 604-sphere configuration was reached after 11 April 2026. The write-up is arXiv:2606.10402 (Bianchi, Kwon, Pappu, Zou), v1 9 Jun 2026, v2 26 Aug 2026.
events.revisions: Blog published 13 Apr 2026 (page read). arXiv 2606.10402: v1 9 Jun 2026; v2 26 Aug 2026, 'Updated to correct a mistake' (what was corrected is not stated).

events.what_happened: Rustem Takhanov and Stanislav Yun, 'Classification of independent sets in signed Johnson graphs and applications to kissing arrangements' (arXiv:2606.03299). Finds 1,579 non-isomorphic maximum independent sets in the signed Johnson graph J±(12,4), each giving a non-isometric kissing arrangement of size 840 in R^12. The abstract does not claim a new lower or upper bound.
events.revisions: Single version v1, 2 Jun 2026 (abstract page read).
events.delivers: Structural: a classification of the maximum independent sets that give 840-point kissing arrangements in R^12. Does not raise any bound on k(12) and does not settle it.

events.direction: Neutral with respect to the bound: a structural classification of 840-point arrangements in dimension 12.
events.object: 1,579 non-isomorphic maximum independent sets in J±(12,4), each corresponding to a non-isometric kissing arrangement of 840 points in R^12 (per the abstract). Not read in detail.

events.what_happened: Rustem Takhanov, Zhenisbek Assylbekov and Stanislav Yun, 'Structure of kissing arrangements in R^12 and a place for the 841st sphere' (arXiv:2606.18984). Gives a spherical code of 841 vectors in R^12 with maximal inner product 0.499999937751 (below 1/2), found numerically by logarithmic Riesz energy minimisation (Adam, 64 batches) from a structured start: the 840 arrangement with one vector appended. The 840 arrangement comes from a 60+60+720 structure built from the unique 1-factorisation of K6.
events.revisions: Single version v1, 17 Jun 2026 (full text read).
events.delivers: Lower bound 841 in dimension 12 (from 840). Lower bound only, one dimension. The 841 configuration is numerical rather than explicit in the paper: the Gram matrix is said to be in a GitHub repository.
events.remains: Exact k(12) (upper bound 1355) and every other dimension in scope.
events.directly_checkable: The 841 vectors are in a repository, not in the paper. A reader could compute the maximum inner product in exact arithmetic; the paper gives only the floating-point value.
events.doubts: The claim rests on floating-point optimisation. The margin below 1/2 is about 6 x 10^-8 in the authors' own number (0.499999937751), and the paper contains no exact verification. The 841 record is also cited by Cohn's table and the 2026 follow-up on the quaternionic construction, which adds structure but no new bound.
events.direction: Lower-bound side only, dimension 12. Moves the bound on k(12) without settling it. Numerical, non-explicit.
events.object: A numerical spherical code of 841 unit vectors in R^12 with pairwise inner products at most 0.499999937751, i.e. a kissing arrangement of size 841 (per the authors). Non-constructive in the sense of not being given in closed form; coordinates in a repository.

events.what_happened: Rustem Takhanov, 'A quaternionic construction behind 841-point kissing arrangement in R^12' (arXiv:2609.09179). Gives a structural description of the 841 record: R^12 viewed as H^3, a new 840-point arrangement built from three orthogonal 24-cells and two 384-point families, and an argument that the 840 arrangement is a structural model of the 841 record. Also defines a general quaternionic construction and checks that record arrangements in R^(4k) for k at most 5 admit one.
events.revisions: Single version v1. Its submission date is in conflict between sources: the abstract page reads 'Submitted 25 Aug 2026', the identifier 2609 indicates September 2026, and the PDF metadata reads 10 Sep 2026. The month is therefore not pinned down.
events.delivers: No new bound: a structural description of the 841 arrangement and of an 840 arrangement. Does not change any kissing-number bound.
events.remains: Every bound question in the problem, including exact k(12).
events.directly_checkable: The 840-point arrangement is explicit in the structure described (three orthogonal 24-cells and two 384-point families); I did not check it.
events.direction: Neutral with respect to any bound. Structural only.
events.object: An explicit 840-point kissing arrangement in R^12 built from three orthogonal 24-cells and two 384-point families (per the abstract); the 841 record is said to be a deformation of it.

events.what_happened: Rustem Takhanov and Stanislav Yun, 'New lower bounds for kissing numbers in dimensions 25-31' (arXiv:2609.21591). Uses PackingStar's saved runs as starting points for a Leech-lifting construction, with a sequential linear programming method with a trust region for the searches. Claims tau25 at least 197058, tau26 at least 198552, tau27 at least 200046, tau28 at least 204522, tau29 at least 209497, tau30 at least 220442, tau31 at least 238354. Searches for dimensions 25, 30 and 31 were unsuccessful in Section III; the final constructions for 25, 30 and 31 come from later sections (an analytic lifting-height change for 25, a deformation plus search for 30, a rotation-based search for 31).
events.revisions: v1 18 Sep 2026; v2 23 Sep 2026 (current; full text read).
events.delivers: Lower bounds in dimensions 25 to 31 only (the values above). No exact value; the authors say their searches do not establish nonexistence of further points.
events.remains: Exact k(n) in dimensions 25 to 31 and every other dimension in scope. Later repositories report higher values in dimensions 25 to 31 (see disputes).
events.directly_checkable: Coordinate files and certificates are said to be in https://github.com/k-nic/Leech_lifting (not opened).
events.doubts: The results build on PackingStar's runs, so they inherit PackingStar's construction and its lack of optimality proofs. The method is an LP search and a lifting construction, not AI. Dimension 25's new value comes from a +2 change to a lifted configuration (197056 to 197058 per the paper).
events.direction: Lower-bound side only, dimensions 25 to 31. Moves bounds on the problem's quantity without settling it; superseded in every dimension by later values in the Kravatskiy repository.

systems.name: PackingStar
systems.what_it_did: Its saved runs supply the starting configurations for the authors' lifting and LP-search constructions in dimensions 25 to 31. The authors' own search method is sequential linear programming, not an AI system. The paper also cites AlphaEvolve and collaborative AI agents as prior work in dimension 11.

events.what_happened: Shuxing Yang, Rui Zhao et al. (16 authors; Zhejiang University affiliation; Qiushi Engine Team), 'Large-Scale Autonomous Discovery of Kissing Number Constructions' (arXiv:2609.35051, cs.IT). States that Qiushi Engine, 'an autonomous multi-agent research system', carried out the construction searches, mathematical analysis and computational verification. Claims lower bounds in 19 dimensions (25, 27, 32 to 39, 43, 45, 49 to 55). Explicit values stated in the abstract: 25: 197580; 27: 201567; 38: 591900; 43: 2553792; 45: 7380090; 55: 53301140. Dimension 25 is stated as one more than the comparison value 197579. disputes.summary: Dimension 25. The Cohn table (read through a summariser) and the Wikipedia table (last edited 10 Oct 2026) both give 197583, and the table's reference list credits Takhanov and Yun (2026). The Takhanov-Yun paper (v2) gives 197058 and its body gives 197056 to 197058. The Kravatskiy repository gives 197579 and says its result is 'a decode, not a correction'. The Qiushi paper gives 197580 and treats 197579 as the comparison. The value 197583 appears in no source I opened. I could not resolve it.

Dimension 27. The Kravatskiy headline table gives 201566 and its run table gives 201509 for verify27.py. Qiushi claims 201567 and says it is +1 over the checked Kravatskiy baseline. The Cohn table (summary read) gives 201589 for dimension 27, which matches none of these. The Takhanov-Yun paper gives 200046 for dimension 27.

Cohn table dimensions 26, 28, 29, 30 and 31 (199868, 205172, 210473, 222072, 241077 as read through a summariser) match none of the papers or repositories I opened for those dimensions (Takhanov-Yun: 198552, 204522, 209497, 220442, 238354; Kravatskiy: 199806, 204896, 209968, 221012, 238662). Its credits for 28 to 31 go to 'K. Li (2026)', whose repository I did not find. The summariser may have misread the table; the raw page should be checked.

Dimension 19. Ho (11 Mar 2026, GPT-5.4 Pro in acknowledgements) gives 11948. The Felpix-Studios repository (Kevin Li, 2026; GPT-6-Astra Pro and Claude Opus 5.5 credited in the README) gives 12276 and is the value the Cohn table and the Wikipedia table show. The Kravatskiy repository makes no dimension-19 claim. Both 11948 and 12276 are recorded as separate events; the two are not reconciled in any source I read, and the 12276 repository has no date and no paper.

Dimension 21 history. Cohn-Li 29768 (Nov 2024), then Kevin Li's 30779 (2026, undated), then Griffin Long's 31259 (9 Oct 2026), 31272 and 31288 (10 Oct 2026). The Wikipedia table (last edited 10 Oct 2026, 07:15 UTC) shows 31272 and the Cohn table (read later) shows 31288. This is table lag, not a conflict in the sources, but the Wikipedia value is outdated by the Long repository's 10 Oct update.

PackingStar's claims differ between versions. The v3 full text read says 'PackingStar surpasses the lower bounds reported in 2016 and also exceeds the construction form introduced in 2011' and 'strictly larger kissing configurations in all dimensions from 25 to 31'. A search snippet describes v2 as beating all human-known records from 25 to 31, and v3 as reproducing all known configurations up to dimension 31 (not read by me). The 13-dimensional claim in a search snippet calls the 1146 configuration a 'first breakthrough beyond rational structures'; the v3 text says only that it beats the 1971 rational record of 1130, while the 1999 non-rational 1154 is not surpassed. The later text is the one used in this record.

Ho's v1 and v2 acknowledgements differ in wording. v2 (as fetched) says 'GPT-5.4 Pro was used in the discovery of the construction and in revising the exposition.' v1 (as fetched) says 'GPT-5.4 Pro was used to discover the construction of this paper, as well as to assist with exposition.' Both fetches went through a summariser, so the exact text needs checking against the PDF.
The whataifound registry grades the AlphaEvolve dimension-11 result 'Independently checked' while stating 'Nobody outside the lab has checked this yet' on the same page.

Aalto's press release (republished by HIIT, 23 Oct 2025) presents Ganzhinov's 2022 preprint results as 'besting AI' in dimensions 10 and 14, while AlphaEvolve's 593 in dimension 11 is one higher than Ganzhinov's 592 (the 2022 preprint). The 'beats AI in two dimensions' framing rests on AlphaEvolve's table entries for dimensions 10 and 14, which I did not read (the colour-coded table was lost in the text version). The 592 in dimension 11 was a 2022 preprint and predates AlphaEvolve's 2025 announcement.

Takhanov's quaternionic paper (arXiv:2609.09179): the abstract page gives 25 Aug 2026 as the submission date, the identifier 2609 indicates September 2026, and the PDF metadata reads 10 Sep 2026. Recorded at year precision.

summary: Since 26 January 2024 the kissing number has moved in many dimensions outside {1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 24}, but no value outside that set has been determined. The in-window bound changes, by date: the upper bound in dimension 6 to 77 (de Laat, Leijenhorst and de Muinck Keizer, April 2024; the abstract was read); the Cohn-Li lower bounds in dimensions 17 to 21 (Nov 2024; read in full, with a v3 AI sentence saying 'Artificial intelligence played no role in these discoveries' and that 'GPT-5.6 Sol helped proofread the paper and write code for the supplementary data', and a thanks to OpenAI for a ChatGPT Pro subscription); AlphaEvolve's 593 in dimension 11 (14 May 2025 announcement; the authors' own write-up names AlphaEvolve); PackingStar's records in dimensions 25 to 31 and a rational 1146 in dimension 13 (17 Nov 2025; authors name a multi-agent RL system); Ho's 11948 in dimension 19 (11 Mar 2026; the authors' acknowledgements name GPT-5.4 Pro); EinsteinArena agents' 604 in dimension 11 (13 Apr 2026 blog; the write-up names no model); Takhanov et al.'s numerical 841 in dimension 12 (17 Jun 2026; no AI); Takhanov and Yun's 25 to 31 values (18 Sep 2026; they use PackingStar's runs as starting points); Kravatskiy's repository with 18 and 25 to 31 (from 17 Sep 2026; 'developed by the author working with Claude Code'); a repository by Kevin Li with 19 and 21 (2026, undated; GPT-6-Astra Pro and Claude Opus 5.5 credited); Qiushi Engine's 19-dimension paper with explicit values in 25, 27, 38, 43, 45, 55 (28 Sep 2026; authors say the system ran the searches and the mathematical analysis); and Griffin Long's repository with 31288 in dimension 21 (9 and 10 Oct 2026; agent-afk, gpt-6.1-sol and Claude Opus named in its README). Structural papers with no new bound are Takhanov-Yun (classification, June 2026) and Takhanov (quaternionic, 2026). Close calls: (a) whether the lower-bound moves count, since the problem asks for exact values and no event determines any k(n); I recorded each as a bound move on the problem's own quantity. (b) Which AI credits are load-bearing: Ho, AlphaEvolve, PackingStar, Qiushi Engine and Takhanov-Yun's use of PackingStar name the system and the authors describe a role in the construction; Kravatskiy, Kevin Li and Griffin Long name tools or models only in READMEs, and I have not confirmed those READMEs' wording beyond the fetch summaries; EinsteinArena names no model. (c) Verification: no journal-level or expert written check of any post-2024 value was found except through GitHub users (carlostoledo1891 reproduced exact pairwise checks for Kravatskiy's dimension 18 and Qiushi's dimensions 25, 27, 43 and 45); the Qiushi check excludes moment certificates and dimensions 32 to 39 and 49 to 55 are unchecked; the Felpix repository has Lean theorems proved by native_decide that I did not check for sorry. (d) Unreconciled values: the dimension 25 value 197583 in the Cohn and Wikipedia tables, the dimension 27 value 201509 versus 201566 in one repository, and the Cohn table's 26, 28 to 31 values, which match no paper I opened. Searches for Lean formalisations of kissing numbers in general, for FunSearch or Gemini results, and for any other AI system credited with a kissing construction found nothing beyond the events above. No upper bound in dimensions other than 6 moved inside the window in any source I found.
competing_reading: Read narrowly, the problem asks for the exact value of k(n) in each dimension outside {1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 24}. Every event here moves only a lower bound, or (dimension 6) an upper bound, and none determines a value, so the status is 'open, with bounds moved' everywhere. On that reading the AI-credited bound moves (AlphaEvolve, PackingStar, Ho, Qiushi, the Kevin Li repository, Griffin Long, Kravatskiy, EinsteinArena) are AI-involved progress on lower bounds only, and the only in-window upper bound move (dimension 6, 2024) involves no AI. Read broadly, the quantity named in the statement is k(n) itself, and its lower bound is half of what the question is about, so each bound move in a named dimension counts as progress on the question; on that reading the AI share is much larger, because most in-window bound moves in dimensions 11, 19, 21, 25 to 31 are credited to AI systems by their authors.
what_would_settle_it: For each event's status: a matching upper and lower bound in some dimension outside {1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 24} would be the only exact result; no such matching is in any source I found. For the AI credits: the authors' own statements for the Kevin Li and Griffin Long repositories and for Kravatskiy in a peer-reviewed or arXiv version, and a verbatim check of the README quotes (they were read through a summariser). For the values: the raw Cohn table and its reference list (to resolve dimension 25 at 197583 against 197579, 197580 and 197058), and an exact all-pairs check of the Qiushi 32 to 39 and 49 to 55 sets. For dates: the arXiv abstract page of 2609.09179 and the first commit of the Kravatskiy and Felpix repositories.

dead_ends: No Lean or Coq formalisation of kissing numbers in general turned up in search (query 19); the only Lean material found is the Felpix-Studios repository, which surfaced through the dimension-19 and dimension-21 searches, not through the Lean search.

No FunSearch, Gemini Deep Think or OpenAI-announced kissing-number result was found (queries 17, 18). The sphere-packing density work (OpenAI's Astra) is a different problem and was not researched here.

No kissing construction credited to Claude in an arXiv paper or the whataifound registry was found (query 23). The Claude credits found are in GitHub READMEs (Kravatskiy; Felpix-Studios and griffinwork40 via the Opus lane) and are recorded under their events.
The name 'Qiushi' returned unrelated results in tracker searches (query 37). The Qiushi Engine paper itself is recorded as its own event.

The 18, 19 and 21 attributions in the Cohn and Wikipedia tables ('Kravatskiy', 'K. Li', 'G. Long') could not be found by name in searches; they were resolved by opening the repositories named in the table's references.
The arXiv listing for a 2026 paper by 'G. Long' was not found; the dimension-21 result exists only as the griffinwork40 repository.
Dimensions 13 to 16 showed no in-window change in any source read: the Cohn table still gives 1154, 1932, 2564 and 4320 (query 24). The 13-dimensional 1146 configuration is rational and below 1154.
The Lasserre-hierarchy follow-up mentioned in a 2024 ISMP abstract (query 8 results) was not chased; it may be a further in-window upper-bound event.
The conic optimisation table (arXiv 2510.06960) and the 2008-era Bachoc-Vallentin and Mittelmann-Vallentin bounds were not opened; they predate the window or are secondary.
